newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease on Yeltsin op,US rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease on Yeltsin op,US rate worries.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell in nervous but low-volume trading on Friday on worries about President Boris Yeltsin's health and fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
The head of the Kremlin medical centre Sergei Mironov said on Friday Yeltsin would stay in hospital for another 3-4 days, facing a "very serious" heart operation.

Dealers said the market was also nervously awaiting next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee Meeting to see if and by how much the U.S. raises interest rates. Dealers were speculating previously on a rise of 25 basis points.
"The market has been overheated recently and all those unsure of the future U.S. credit rates have already sold all emerging market instruments, including MinFins," one dealer said.
Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said concern about the result of Yeltsin's heart surgery was the main depressing factor, although prices were easing on low volumes traded.
"There are no big sales, levels are going down by themselves," he said and added prices had fallen about 1.0 point from the very beginning of trading but then bounced back.
Dealers said the third, fourth and fifth tranches found support at 77.40, 51.40 and 33.50 respectively. The sixth and seventh tranches, issued in May, were not traded actively inside Russia.
